study.title: Mark 9 - Revealed glory, proven faith and discipleship marked by service
study.overview: Mark 9 presents an intense sequence: Jesus anticipates the manifestation of the Kingdom with power, reveals his glory in the transfiguration, teaches that his mission goes through suffering and calls the disciples to a faith dependent on God. Then he confronts the disaidness of the disciples in the face of a case of spiritual oppression, corrects ambition for greatness, receives the service made in his name and closes with solemn warnings against sin, the scandal and the loss of the spiritual "sal." The chapter shows that true greatness in the Kingdom does not appear in prestige, but in obedience, prayer, humility, care for small and peace among the brethren.

outline.title: The Transfiguration and the Testimony of the Father
outline.explanation: Jesus promises that some gifts would see the Kingdom of God coming with power. Shortly afterward, he takes Peter, James and John to a mountain and transfigures himself before them. Moses and Elijah appear talking to Jesus, and the voice of the cloud confirms his identity: he is the beloved Son, whom the disciples should hear. As they descend, Jesus orders silence until the resurrection, and the disciples are confused about the language of the "resuscitate of the dead" and about the relationship between Elijah and the coming of the Son of man.

outline.title: The healing of the child and the need for faith and prayer
outline.explanation: Upon returning to the other disciples, Jesus finds dispute with scribes and a crowd stirred because of a boy oppressed by a dumb spirit. The disciples cannot expel him, and Jesus denounces the unbelief of the present generation. The boy's father expresses a faith mixed with weakness: he believes, but asks for help for his unbelief. Jesus frees the child with authority, and then explains to the disciples that that kind of oppression does not come out without prayer and fasting.

outline.title: The way of the cross, humility and generosity in the name of Christ
outline.explanation: Jesus resumes teaching in particular, announcing that the Son of man will be delivered, killed and risen on the third day, although the disciples do not understand. Then confront the conversation about who would be the greatest and teaches that the first should be the last and servant of all. By placing a child in the middle, Jesus shows that receiving the little ones in his name is to receive Christ himself and also the one who sent him. Then corrects John: whoever performs works in his name should not be prevented if he is not against him, and even a glass of water given because of Christ will be rewarded.

outline.title: Warning against scandal and exhortation to inner purity
outline.explanation: Jesus warns severely against leading to sin one of the little ones who believe in him. Then he uses strong images about hand, foot and eye to show the radical need to abandon what leads to sin, for the fate of sin is the fire that does not go out. The teaching ends with the image of the salt: each one will be robbed with fire, the sacrifices will have salt, and the disciples must keep salt in themselves and live in peace with one another.

study.context: The chapter records the continuation of Jesus" ministry in Galilee and then in Capernaum. There are scribes discussing with the disciples, and the disciples travel with Jesus by the way, which highlights the environment of instruction during the displacement. The notes also associate the transfiguration with a high hill, but do not fix for sure what this hill was. The text also shows that the disciples already participated in the mission of casting out demons, although here they fail and need to be re-taught by Jesus.
study.theology: Mark 9 unites revelation and cross. The glory of Jesus in the transfiguration does not annul, but confirms his identity as a beloved Son and anticipation of his future glory. At the same time, the chapter insists that the path of the Messiah undergoes suffering, rejection, death, and resurrection. True faith is not self-confidence, but humble dependence: "I believe it; it helps me in my unbelief" well summarizes the kind of faith that the text approves. It is also clear that spiritual authority is neither technical nor status; it is God-dependent exercise, expressed in prayer, fasting, and submission to the word of Christ. In discipleship, greatness is service, welcoming the little ones and peace between brothers and sisters. Finally, warnings about sin show that holiness requires serious decision and radical renunciation, because the Kingdom of God does not relativize evil, but calls a preserved life, as salt that has not lost its taste.

scholarViews.insight: The promise that some would see the coming Kingdom with power is most likely fulfilled in the transfiguration, put by Mark shortly after the announcement.
The transfiguration shows the Kingdom of God approaching with power and confirms the manifestation of Christ's glory before chosen witnesses.
The lack of success of the disciples in this case highlights that expulsion depended on a type of intervention that required prayer and fasting.

questions: What changes in the way you see Jesus when you read the transfiguration alongside the proclamation of suffering and resurrection?
In which areas of life do you look like the child's father, real creing, but still needing Jesus" help against his own unbelief?
What practical attitude today would you show that you understand greatness in the Kingdom as a service, the reception of the little ones and peace with the brothers and sisters?
study.practice: This week, practice three concrete steps: first, set aside time for sincere prayer, without pretending faith greater than yours; second, make an act of discreet service by someone "little" or little noticed in the community; third, abandon a practice, image, habit or word that is leading you to sin, taking seriously the warnings of Jesus. End every day seeking "salt in yourself" through repentance, gratitude, and reconciliation with someone, if there is conflict.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided recognize that the fulfillment of Mark 9:1 is debated between several readings, although they indicate the transfiguration as more likely. They also do not allow you to safely determine which was the mount of the transfiguration. Some relations between Elijah, the restoration and suffering of the Son of Man remain summarized in the text itself without detailed explanation in the notes, and should be read with caution.
